title: Death at Ashcombe Manor
summary: Lord Edmund Ashcombe was found dead in his study at 10pm, struck down with his own silver letter opener. Four people were in the house that night, and each of them had a reason to be somewhere they should not have been.

victim.name: Lord Edmund Ashcombe
victim.description: The master of the manor, wealthy, sharp-tongued, and about to rewrite his will.

suspects.name: Mr. Hobbs
suspects.description: The butler, thirty years in service and loyal to a fault.

suspects.name: Clara Ashcombe
suspects.description: The victim's niece, who stood to lose her inheritance under the new will.

suspects.name: Dr. Alistair Finch
suspects.description: The family physician, a guest for the weekend with debts he never mentions.

suspects.name: Mrs. Pike
suspects.description: The cook, who misses nothing that happens below stairs.

planned_lies.says: I was reading in the library all evening. I never went near my uncle's study.

clues.description: Mrs. Pike was in the kitchen at 10pm, plating the late supper.
At 10pm Mrs. Pike saw Mr. Hobbs come in for the supper tray.
The pavilion visitors' book has Dr. Finch signed in from 9:55pm to 10:40pm.
A torn diary page in Clara's hand says she went to the study at ten.
The empty case of the letter opener was found in Clara's dressing table.
Lord Ashcombe's ledger records a large loan to Dr. Finch, still unpaid.

documents.title: Garden pavilion visitors' book
documents.body: Saturday. 9:55pm, Dr. A. Finch, in. 10:40pm, Dr. A. Finch, out. Remarks: lamp left burning.

documents.title: Torn diary page
documents.body: He will not listen. At ten I am going to the study to have it out with him, whatever it costs me.

documents.title: Housekeeper's note on the letter opener case
documents.body: Found the velvet case for His Lordship's silver letter opener in Miss Clara's dressing table, empty.

documents.title: Page from Lord Ashcombe's ledger
documents.body: Loan to Dr. A. Finch, two thousand pounds, due at Michaelmas. Not repaid. Raise this with him on Saturday.

documents.title: Saturday dinner menu
documents.body: Dinner at eight. Clear oxtail soup, sole meuniere, saddle of mutton, apple charlotte. Cold game pie and claret for the late supper tray at ten.

documents.title: Staff duties for Saturday
documents.body: Mr. Hobbs: wine, silver, and the ballroom lamps. Mrs. Pike: dinner and the late supper. Ellen, housemaid: night off, gone to her sister's in the village.

documents.title: Hall barometer readings
documents.body: Saturday morning, glass steady at 30.1. Evening, glass falling, wind south-west. Light rain expected overnight.

documents.title: Letter from the family solicitor
documents.body: My Lord, the revised will is drawn as you instructed and will be ready for your signature on Monday. The residue passes to the Cottage Hospital and not to Miss Ashcombe. I would urge you, once more, to tell her before you sign. Yours faithfully, R. Dunmore.

documents.title: Telegram for Dr. Finch
documents.body: DR A FINCH CARE OF ASHCOMBE MANOR. YOUR ACCOUNT NOW SIX MONTHS IN ARREARS. SETTLEMENT EXPECTED BY MONDAY OR WE PROCEED. HARGREAVE AND SONS.

documents.title: Contents of Dr. Finch's medical bag
documents.body: Stethoscope. Thermometer in case. Two rolls of lint. Phial of laudanum, half full. A pawnbroker's ticket for a gold half-hunter watch, folded in the lining.

documents.title: Grocer's invoice
documents.body: Dawlish and Sons, family grocers, to Mrs. Pike for Ashcombe Manor. Two pounds of best tea, one Stilton, a dozen lemons, six pounds of sugar. Account to be settled quarterly.

documents.title: Library lending register
documents.body: Thursday. Miss C. Ashcombe, The Moonstone, Mr. Collins, volume one. Dr. Finch, Gray's Anatomy, returned. Shelf above the window wants dusting.

documents.title: Clipping from the county paper
documents.body: The Ashcombe Hunt Ball, long a fixture of the season, will not be held this year. Lord Ashcombe is understood to have declined to open the ballroom, citing the expense.

documents.title: Gardener's note on the pavilion
documents.body: Pavilion lamp needs a new wick and the chimney glass is cracked. Paths raked Friday. Roses by the pavilion steps want tying in before the frost.

documents.title: Household breakage book
documents.body: One Wedgwood cup, saucer saved. One pane in the conservatory, cracked by the wind. One wine glass from the ballroom set, chipped at the rim.

documents.title: Ballroom inventory
documents.body: Gilt chairs, forty, stacked under dust sheets. Piano tuned in March. Chandeliers cleaned and lamps trimmed for the weekend.

documents.title: Constable's first report
documents.body: Telephone message received from Ashcombe Manor, Saturday night. Attended and found Lord Ashcombe dead in the study from a wound to the chest. No sign of forced entry. The household detained for questioning.
